item.title: Tips for healthy school lunches your kids will actually eat
item.description: Nora LeTorre, the CEO of Eat Real, joins "CBS Mornings" to share some tips for making your child's school lunches healthier.

item.title: 1 in 3 Americans with health insurance have medical debt, survey finds
item.description: Nearly half of Americans with medical debt owe at least $2,000, forcing them to make tough choices, new research shows.

item.title: NASA astronauts on their monthslong expedition on the International Space Station
item.description: CBS News senior national correspondent Mark Strassmann interviews NASA astronauts Jack Hathaway and Jessica Meir, the current commander of the International Space Station, as they wrap up a more than seven-month expedition aboard the orbiting laboratory. They discuss recent spacewalks, SpaceX's Starship, and what they're looking forward to about returning to Earth.

item.title: U.N. experts say U.S. may have committed war crimes with 2 Iran strikes
item.description: U.N.-commissioned rights experts say there are "reasonable grounds" to believe the U.S. committed war crimes with strikes that killed scores of Iranian civilians.

item.title: Macklemore and Robert Kraft release dueling statements on humanitarian aid donations
item.description: Macklemore called for Robert Kraft to match his $1 million donation to Palestinian humanitarian aid relief organizations, while Kraft said he already matched a donation made by Ed Sheeran. The dueling statements came after Macklemore was dropped from Sheeran's tour for making pro-Palestinian comments onstage. Meg Oliver reports.

item.title: Alicia Keys, Lauryn Hill and Wyclef Jean to perform at 2026 Global Citizen Festival
item.description: The 2026 Global Citizen Festival kicks off in New York City's Central Park in late September. Global Citizen co-founder Hugh Evans explains the charity work his organization does.

item.title: Trump photo shows him viewing "Kennedy Center demolished" document
item.description: In court documents filed Wednesday by Rep. Joyce Beatty, a witness said he saw a "forklift run into and hit the pillars" of the building.

item.title: How much will a $750,000 annuity pay each month in 2026?
item.description: A $750,000 annuity may provide you with a sizable retirement income, but the monthly payout can vary widely.

item.title: Terror groups take advantage of AI developments
item.description: Amid recent warnings by AI leaders over the risks of rapid tech development, Leigh Kiniry reports on how terrorist groups take advantage of AI.

item.title: King Charles leery of "existential dangers" of AI
item.description: Britain's King Charles III hosted a summit with tech leaders about the dangers of artificial intelligence. This comes amid an Anthropic report warning that terror groups have attempted to use Claude to develop weapons. CBS News' Leigh Kiniry reports.

item.title: Video from LA news helicopter prior to crash could hold key to investigation
item.description: The National Transportation Safety Board is investigating the crash of an NBC news helicopter in Los Angeles.

item.title: How the Fed's interest rate increase may impact your finances
item.description: CBS News business analyst Jill Schlesinger explains how the Federal Reserve's interest rate hike for the first time since 2023 could impact Americans.

item.title: Details emerge on Philadelphia house of horrors as missing woman's family wants answers
item.description: Family members are demanding answers about a Philadelphia woman who went missing in 2016 as officials conduct a monthslong search of the "house of horrors" where they believe she was last seen.

item.title: Cyberattacks are a real threat to ports and waterways, Coast Guard official says
item.description: The U.S. is investigating cyberattacks on two energy tankers to determine whether Iran was involved. CBS News' Nicole Sganga has what you need to know.

item.title: How an interest rate hike impacts you
item.description: CBS News business analyst Jill Schlesinger joins to discuss how the interest rate hike will impact Americans' wallets.

item.title: What are today's mortgage interest rates: September 17, 2026?
item.description: The Fed just raised interest rates for the first time since 2023. Here's how mortgage interest rates responded.

item.title: Princess Diana's brother claims Charles told him, "we'll forget her soon"
item.description: The late Prince Diana's brother claims in a new book that King Charles had "contempt" for his ex-wife, telling him she would be forgotten "soon enough."

item.title: Speaker Johnson avoids controversial votes with early House recess
item.description: House Speaker Mike Johnson sent lawmakers home a day early, sidestepping potentially controversial votes before Americans head to the polls in November. CBS News' Nikole Killion reports.

item.title: Trump calls interest rates "artificially high," says they should be "1% or less"
item.description: President Trump lashed out at the Federal Reserve after the central bank voted to raise interest rates by 0.25 percentage points. CBS News' Aaron Navarro has more.

item.title: Princess Diana's brother makes stunning claim about Charles' reaction to her death
item.description: Princess Diana's brother, Earl Spencer, makes stunning allegations in a new memoir against then-Prince Charles, now King Charles III, and his reaction to Diana's death. Holly Williams reports.

item.title: Buckingham Palace hits back at new claims made by Princess Diana's brother in new book
item.description: Princess Diana's brother, Charles Spencer, will soon release his memoir, "Swan Song: Diana, My Sister." Buckingham Palace issued a response to claims made in the book about King Charles III's behavior after Princess Diana's death. CBS News' Holly Williams has context.

item.title: House passes Russia sanctions bill, overcoming Democratic opposition
item.description: The bill was championed by GOP Sen. Lindsey Graham, who died suddenly just one day after announcing a deal had been reached with the White House to move forward.

item.title: AI agents are smart enough to break the law. Who is criminally liable?
item.description: A question of criminal liability has been raised after some companies reported AI models carrying out concerning behavior. The Free Press contributor and Yale Law School professor Jed Rubenfeld shares his thoughts. The Free Press is a Paramount publication.

item.title: House cutting week short before adjourning until after midterms
item.description: House Speaker Mike Johnson canceled votes in the chamber that were planned for Thursday ahead of a six-week recess.

item.title: North Carolina farmer unhappy with Trump amid high energy prices, Fed hike
item.description: The Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 0.25 percentage points, defying President Trump's push to cut them. This comes as the Iran war drives up oil prices and inflation remains high. CBS News' Weijia Jiang reports.

item.title: Millionaires are everywhere in the U.S., new book says
item.description: Getting rich in the U.S. is still possible, but the most common path to wealth doesn't involve working for other people, according to a new book.

item.title: OpenAI reveals 6 more incidents of "unexpected or concerning" AI behavior
item.description: OpenAI has disclosed six reports of "unexpected or concerning" behavior in artificial intelligence models as the debate on AI safety​ becomes increasingly heated.

item.title: House passes bill to shield Americans from data center energy costs
item.description: The vote comes as lawmakers face increasing pressure to respond to the data center boom driven by the AI race.

item.title: Humpback whale seen grieving dead calf in rare footage
item.description: The footage shows a female humpback whale staying close to the dead calf as it lies motionless on the seafloor, touching it with its head and fin.

item.title: Remains of ancient warhorse given honorific burial discovered in Egypt
item.description: Archaeologists say they've discovered the remains of a likely ancient Egyptian warhorse given an honorific burial more than 3,000 years ago.
